# e-Shram Card 2025: Apply Online, Check Benefits & Download Easily

Updated on: 08 Jul, 2026 12:06 PM

[![Follow Tax2Win on Google](https://emailer.tax2win.in/assets/guides/all_guides/google-preferred-source-badge.png)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=tax2win.in)

The Government of India started the e-Shram yojana to provide social security to the workers engaged in the unorganized sector. The government also launched the e-shram portal to collect data of all unorganized workers and provide them with the benefits of government schemes.

Any person working in the unorganized sector can apply for an e-shram card form through which they can get various eshram card benefits such as death insurance, pension after 60 years, and other types of financial aid in case of incapacity. In this article, we will explore the various benefits of an e-shram card, its registration process, and the download process.

### E-Shram Card Updates 2025

As per the 2025 latest update, the Indian government provided a big relief to the taxpayers. It will provide financial assistance of upto Rs. 9000 directly to eligible e-Shram card holders in their bank accounts.

Still not filed your ITR or need to update your already filed ITR? You can still file ITR U for FY 2020-21, FY 2021-22, FY 2022-23, FY 2023-24, & FY 2024-25. [Connect Today!](https://tax2win.in/contact-us)

### Contents

- [What is e-Shram Card?](https://tax2win.in/guide/e-shram-card#What-is-e-Shram-Card)
- [What is Unorganised Sector?](https://tax2win.in/guide/e-shram-card#What-is-the-Unorganised-Sector)
- [What are e-Shram Card Benefits?](https://tax2win.in/guide/e-shram-card#What-are-e-Shram-Card-Benefits)
- [What is the Eligibility Criteria for e-Shram Card?](https://tax2win.in/guide/e-shram-card#What-is-the-Eligibility-Criteria-for-e-Shram-Card)
- [e-Shram Card Registration - How to Apply for e-Shram Card Online?](https://tax2win.in/guide/e-shram-card#e-Shram-Card-Registration-How-to-Apply-for-e-Shram-Card-Online)
- [What are the Documents Required for e-Shram Card?](https://tax2win.in/guide/e-shram-card#What-are-the-Documents-Required-for-e-Shram-Card)
- [How to download e-Shram card](https://tax2win.in/guide/e-shram-card#How-to-download-e-Shram-card)
- [How to Download an Already Registered e-Shram Card?](https://tax2win.in/guide/e-shram-card#How-to-Download-an-Already-Registered-e-Shram-Card)
- [How to check payment status and balance in e-Shram card](https://tax2win.in/guide/e-shram-card#How-to-check-payment-status-and-balance-in-e-Shram-card)
- [How to Get Rs.9000 Financial Assistance?](https://tax2win.in/guide/e-shram-card#How-to-Get-Rs-9000-Financial-Assistance)
- [What is the Application Process for Rs. 9000 Financial Assistance?](https://tax2win.in/guide/e-shram-card#What-is-the-Application-Process-for-Rs-9000-Financial-Assistance)
- [e-Shram Card Helpline Number](https://tax2win.in/guide/e-shram-card#e-Shram-Card-Helpline-Number)
- [FAQs](https://tax2win.in/guide/e-shram-card#faqs)

### Good to Know!

The government plans to register gig workers on the e-Shram portal and provide them with identity cards, recognizing their growing role in the digital economy. Additionally, nearly one crore workers will gain access to healthcare benefits under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY), ensuring better financial and medical security.

* * *

## What is e-Shram Card?

e-Shram is a revolutionary initiative designed to offer a safety net for workers in the unorganized sector. It serves as a comprehensive database that not only registers workers but also facilitates their access to various welfare schemes and benefits.

All unorganized sector workers aged between 16 and 59 years can register for the e-Shram card. This includes individuals working as laborers, daily-wage earners, and others in informal employment. Importantly, you should not be a member of the [Employees' Provident Fund Organization](https://tax2win.in/guide/epfo-provident-fund) (EPFO)/Employee State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) or the [National Pension Scheme](https://tax2win.in/guide/nps-national-pension-scheme) (NPS).

* * *

## What is Unorganised Sector?

The unorganized sector consists of the units or establishments engaged in the production or sale of goods and services and has employed less than 10 workers. These units should not be covered under the EPFO and ESIC Act. Employees working in companies classified as unorganized sector can apply for e-shram cards.

* * *

## What are e-Shram Card Benefits?

An e-shram card will provide the employees of the unorganized sector with the following benefits -

- A pension of Rs.3000 per month after reaching the age of 60 years.
- A death insurance of Rs.2,00,000 and financial aid of Rs.1,00,000 if the worker is partially handicapped.
- If the beneficiary of the e-shram card dies, the benefits are given to his/her spouse.
- The beneficiaries will also receive a 12-digit UAN number, which is valid throughout India.

* * *

## What is the Eligibility Criteria for e-Shram Card?

- Any person working in the unorganized sector is eligible for an e-shram card.
- The worker should be 16-59 years old.
- The workers should have their mobile number linked with the Aadhaar card.

* * *

## e-Shram Card Registration - How to Apply for e-Shram Card Online?

The e-Shram card application can be submitted either through the Common Service Centre (CSC) or the e-Shram portal. Those eligible can visit the nearest CSC center to apply for the e-Shram card, and the e-Shram portal helps locate the nearest CSC center by entering the state and district information.

The online application process for obtaining the e-Shram card is outlined below:

- Go to the e-Shram portal's self-registration page.
- Input the Aadhaar-linked mobile number, captcha code, and click 'Send OTP.'
- Receive the OTP on the registered mobile number and enter it, then click 'Validate.'
- Confirm the personal details present on the screen.
- Provide necessary information, including address and educational qualifications.
- Choose the skill name, and specify the nature of the business and type of work.
- Enter bank details and select self-declaration.
- Click 'Preview' to review the entered details, then click 'Submit.'
- Receive another OTP, enter it, and click 'Verify.'
- The e-Shram card is generated and displayed on the screen.
- Optionally, download the e-Shram card by clicking on the download option.

* * *

## What are the Documents Required for e-Shram Card?

The following documents are required for an e-shram card -

- Aadhaar Card
- Bank Account
- Mobile number linked with Aadhaar card

* * *

## How to download e-Shram card

After submitting the e-shram card application, proceed with the steps below to download the card:

- Go to the e-Shram portal.
- Click on the 'Already Registered' tab and choose the option to 'Update/download UAN card.'
- Provide the date of birth, UAN number, and captcha code, and click 'Generate OTP.'
- Enter the OTP received on your mobile and click 'Validate.'
- Confirm the displayed personal details.
- Click on 'Preview' to review the entered details, and then click 'Submit.'
- Receive another OTP, enter it, and click 'Verify.'
- The e-Shram card is generated and shown on the screen.
- At this time, you can download the e-Shram card by clicking on the download option.

* * *

## How to Download an Already Registered e-Shram Card?

- Visit the e-shram portal and click on the tab named ‘already registered.’
- Select the ‘Update/download UAN card’ option.
- Provide the details required, like the UAN number, captcha code, and date of birth. Now, click on ‘generate OTP.’
- Submit the OTP received on the mobile number and click on ‘validate.’
- Confirm these details. Click on ‘Preview’ and check the details. Now, click on submit.
- Submit the OTP received on your mobile number to complete OTP verification. Now, click on verify.
- The e-shram card is generated, and you can click on the download option.

* * *

## How to Check Payment Status and Balance in e-Shram Card

Follow the below steps to check the remaining balance and the payment status in your e-Shram card:

- Visit the [e-Shram portal](https://eshram.gov.in/).
- Click on the **'E-Aadhaar Card Beneficiary Status Check'** link.
- Enter the e-Shram card number, UAN number, or Aadhar Card.
- Click the **'Submit'** button.
- Review the e-Shram payment status displayed on the page.

* * *

## How to Get Rs.9000 Financial Assistance?

The government is giving financial assistance to workers in installments. This amount is transferred directly to their bank accounts through the DBT (Direct Benefit Transfer) system.

To receive this benefit, individuals must first register for an e-Shram card. They can complete the registration by visiting the official website or their nearest CSC (Common Service Center) using their Aadhaar-linked mobile number.

* * *

## What is the Application Process for Rs. 9000 Financial Assistance?

In order to get Rs. 9000 financial assistance, you must first register for the e-shram card after carefully reviewing whether you are eligible for the same -

- **Visit the official e-Shram portal** and click on **“REGISTER on e-Shram”.**
- **Enter your Aadhaar-linked mobile number** and the captcha code.
- **Verify the OTP** received on your mobile.
- **Fill in your details** such as name, address, occupation type, and bank account information.
- **Submit the form** to receive your **12-digit UAN (Universal Account Number).**
- **Download your e-Shram card** and keep it safe for future use.

* * *

## e-Shram Card Helpline Number

For any queries related to e-Shram card, you can contact the office at the toll-free helpdesk number available at 14434 / 1800 889 6811, daily from 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM (including Sundays), providing support in Hindi, English, Tamil, Bengali, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Odia, Telugu, and Assamese.

The e-Shram Card initiative by the government of India is a crucial step that will make the government benefits more accessible to the unorganized sector employees. The simplified online application process through the e-Shram portal empowers individuals to access these benefits seamlessly.

Missed the ITR filing deadline, received a notice, or have any other tax-related query? Get in touch with our tax experts who can help you with everything related to taxes, GST, company registration, HUF registration or e-shram card. [Connect with experts now!](https://tax2win.in/contact-us)

* * *

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Q\- What is the UAN number of the e-Shram card?

The unique Universal Account Number (UAN) issued by the government is linked to the e-SHRAM card, a vital document in the Shramik Yojana. To access various benefits, individuals must enroll and obtain their 12-digit UAN.

* * *

### Q\- How to check 1000 rupees in an eShram card?

To confirm the ₹1000 credited to your eShram card, simply login to the eShram portal, navigate to the 'Transactions' tab and review your transaction history for the credited amount.

* * *

### Q\- How can I download a UAN card?

- **Step 1:** Go to the EPFO portal.
- **Step 2:** Sign in by providing your UAN, password, and captcha code.
- **Step 3:** Select the 'UAN Card' option.

* * *

### Q\- How can I check my UAN card status?

- **Step 1.** Go to the EPFO homepage and click on 'For Employees.'
- **Step 2.** Choose 'Member UAN/Online Service,' followed by 'Know UAN status.'
- **Step 3.** Enter your details, request an OTP, and follow the instructions to get your UAN.

* * *

### Q\- How do I check eligibility for my e-Shram card?

Any unorganized sector workers aged between 16 and 59, such as laborers and daily-wage earners, can apply for the e-Shram card. However, they must not be enrolled in EPFO/ESIC or NPS memberships.

# e-Shram Card Benefits, Eligibility, Advantages and Disadvantages

[![Tejas Jain's avatar](https://www.bimakavach.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/cropped-Tejas_Bangalore-40x40.png)](https://www.bimakavach.com/blog/author/tejas/)

[Toggle](https://www.bimakavach.com/blog/e-shram-card-apply-online-benefits-eligibility-india/#)

Understanding the e-Shram card benefits is the first step for India’s unorganised workforce to gain access to social security and Government welfare schemes.  The e-Shram card scheme was introduced by the Ministry of Labour and Employment in 2021. It offers every registered worker a unique 12-digit Universal Account Number (UAN) and the much-needed access to schemes like PMSBY accident insurance.

This guide explains what the e-Shram card is, who is eligible to apply, its advantages and disadvantages, and why employers who hire unorganised and contract workers should also consider [Workmen’s Compensation Insurance](https://www.bimakavach.com/workmens-compensation-insurance/) to meet the gaps left by the e-Shram card.

* * *

## Key Takeaways

- The e-Shram card provides the unorganised workers in India with a UAN-based digital identity and access to schemes such as PMSBY accident insurance and DBT-linked welfare.
- Workers aged 16 to 59 in the unorganised sector and not covered by EPFO or ESIC are eligible to register for an e-Shram card for free.
- The card has certain limitations. Workers in the formal sector are not covered, and technology/documentation gaps can still keep vulnerable workers out.
- e-Shram is designed to cover worker identity and limited accident insurance. It does not cover an employer’s legal liability for workplace injuries, and this is where Workmen’s Compensation Insurance steps in.

* * *

## What is the e-Shram Card Scheme?

The e-Shram card scheme is the official registration system of the Indian Government for unorganised sector workers. It is focused on understanding the e-Shram card benefits and extending social security to the vast informal workforce in the country. Started by the Ministry of Labour and Employment in August 2021, the e-Shram portal initiated the National Database for Unorganised Workers (NDUW). This is India’s first centralised database of workers outside the ambit of formal employment structures. As per current data, over 29 crore workers have registered on the portal.

Every registered worker is granted an e-Shram card that carries a unique 12-digit Universal Account Number (UAN), which is valid all over India (regardless of which part of the country the worker moves to for employment). The UAN is the digital backbone that gives informal workers a verified identity within the Government’s welfare ecosystem and links them to different welfare schemes, insurance coverage, and social security benefits,

## Important Features of the e-SHRAM Card

The e-SHRAM Card is a valuable instrument for the unorganised workforce in India because it has several important features such as:

- **Universal Account Number (UAN):** Each registered worker is provided with a 12-digit number, which is valid throughout his or her life.
- **Nationwide Validity:** The card is valid throughout India, and even in cases when workers change their workplace to take a job, the benefits are portable.
- **Digital Database:** The portal maintains a real-time database of unorganised workers, including gig and platform workers.
- **Financial Assistance:** Workers are directly linked to government benefits through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) system.
- **Free Accident Insurance:** Registered workers automatically receive insurance coverage under the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY).

These features collectively help workers gain visibility, financial security, and easier access to welfare schemes.

## Who All Can Apply for the e-Shram Card?

e-Shram card eligibility is built specifically around India’s informal workforce, covering millions of workers who fall outside traditional employment protections.

**Definition of Unorganised Workers**

Under the Unorganised Workers’ Social Security Act, 2008, an unorganised worker is anyone who is self-employed or works in an unregistered enterprise. Also, he does not fall under the umbrella of the Factories Act/similar labour legislation and is not covered under ESIC or EPFO.

**Examples of Eligible Workers**

- App-based delivery and ride-hailing workers (a fast-growing segment of the e-shram card for unorganised workers base)
- Agricultural labourers and farmhands
- Construction workers and daily wage earners
- Domestic helpers and cleaners
- Street vendors and hawkers
- Freelancers and other gig economy workers
- Small shop workers, barbers, tailors, and similar trades

**Eligibility Criteria**

- **Age:** Between 16 and 59 years
- **Employment type:** Working in the unorganised sector
- **Aadhaar requirement:** A valid Aadhaar number linked to an active mobile number
- **Bank account:** An active bank account to receive benefits through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)

**One important point to note**: As the scheme is only for the unorganised workforce, those workers already registered under EPFO or ESIC generally are not allowed to register on the e-Shram portal.

## How to Register for an e-Shram Card and Documents Required

[e-Shram registration](https://www.bimakavach.com/blog/e-shram-card-registration-benefits-status-download/) is free for all and can be done online using the e-Shram portal or offline at a Common Service Centre(CSC) near you. The CSC staff can help with data entry and verification. Before you start the process, please keep the following documents and details ready:

- **Aadhaar card**: Must be linked to one of your active mobile numbers
- **Bank account details**: Including the account number and IFSC code, to enable benefit transfers in future
- **Aadhaar-linked mobile number**: An OTP will be sent to this number for verification
- **Personal details**: Name, occupation, and address

After completing the registration process, the e-Shram card is generated instantly. You can download or print it at your convenience.

## Advantages of the e-Shram Card

Here are some of the most important e-Shram card benefits you should be aware of:

1. **Insurance Coverage:** Registered workers can get free accidental insurance under the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY). They will receive ₹2 lakh for accidental death/complete disability, and ₹1 lakh for partial disability.

2. **Direct Access to Government Schemes:** As each worker’s UAN is directly linked to schemes such as Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY), Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM), Atal Pension Yojana (APY), and PM-KISAN, it facilitates easy verification and faster disbursal. The Government can identify and directly reach the eligible beneficiaries without duplicate paperwork across different portals.

3. **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT):** Financial benefits and relief (including emergency support during pandemics) are credited directly into the bank account of the worker. There is no involvement of intermediaries.
4. **Future Employment Opportunities:** As the NDUW database expands, it can potentially function as a recruitment and skill-matching tool. Thus, it can help connect registered workers to employers looking for workers with specific skill sets.

5. **Long-Term Social Security:** As time progresses and more welfare schemes are integrated through the e-Shram gateway, the enrolled workers should find it easier to access pension, maternity, and health schemes. This, in turn, would help build a stronger long-term safety net.

## Disadvantages of the e-Shram Card

While the benefits are substantial, you should also know about the e-shram card advantages and disadvantages trade-offs to have a balanced outlook. Here are certain limitations of this card:

1. **Restricted to the Unorganised Sector:** The scheme is designed exclusively for informal workers, so those already employed formally under EPFO or ESIC are not eligible to register.

2. **Possible EPFO/ESIC Conflicts:** If a worker who is already covered under EPFO or ESIC registers by mistake, it can create discrepancies in their records that may need to be corrected later.

3. **Technology Barriers:** Workers without access to a smartphone, stable internet, or basic digital literacy may find online registration difficult, even though CSC support exists.

4. **Data Privacy Considerations:** Since the portal links Aadhaar and personal data in one centralised database, some workers may have concerns about how their information is stored and used.

5. **Not an Automatic Benefit:** The e-Shram card itself is an identity and database entry. It doesn’t automatically grant scheme benefits. Workers still need to check eligibility and enrol separately for each welfare scheme.

6. **Limited Awareness in Rural Areas:** Many eligible workers in remote or rural regions remain unaware of the scheme entirely, which limits its real-world reach despite high registration numbers.


Please note that for eligible workers, the e-Shram card benefits generally outweigh these limitations, and this makes the e-Shram card a positive move toward long-term social security.

## Importance of the e-Shram Card for Unorganised Sector Workers

As nearly 80% of India’s total workforce is engaged in the unorganised sector, a majority of them have been working without job security, health benefits, or formal recognition. The e-Shram card for unorganised workers has made a much-needed paradigm shift here. It has brought millions of gig workers, migrant labourers, and informal wage earners into a unified, recognised system. While this will help policymakers obtain reliable, centralised data to design targeted welfare schemes, workers will also get a verified legal identity and a smoother path to social security. Thus, this shift marks a meaningful step toward dignity, security, and inclusive economic growth.

## How Workmen’s Compensation Insurance Complements the e-Shram Card

The e-Shram card benefits discussed above offer a valuable safety net. However, they can’t provide a comprehensive solution for all the risks faced at the workplace. The PMSBY accident cover tied to e-Shram can only cover accidental death or disability. It doesn’t cover medical treatment costs, wages during temporary disability periods, or the employer’s legal liability toward an injured worker.

This is where a different legal obligation comes in. Under the [Employees’ Compensation Act, 1923,](https://www.bimakavach.com/blog/workmen-compensation-act-1923-understanding-the-key-provisions/) employers are independently liable to compensate workers for injuries, occupational diseases, and death arising out of and during the course of employment. The Act makes employers liable regardless of whether the worker is registered on e-Shram.

[Workmen’s Compensation Insurance](https://www.bimakavach.com/workmens-compensation-insurance/) is designed to cover precisely this liability on the part of the employer. It typically covers medical treatment expenses, death benefits payable to dependents, compensation for temporary and permanent disability, and legal defence costs in case of disputes or claims.

This makes it especially relevant for all employers who engage unorganised/contract workers in sectors such as construction, manufacturing, transport, and logistics, where workers are usually prone to injury while performing their jobs. Therefore, considering the increased emphasis on employer obligations, no one should have any doubt as to [why every employer needs a WC policy](https://www.bimakavach.com/blog/why-every-employer-should-have-a-workmens-compensation-policy-in-place/).

## Simplify Workmen’s Compensation Insurance with BimaKavach

Selecting the right Workmen Compensation Policy for your business doesn’t need to be difficult. In the BimaKavach platform, employers can compare policies from 25+ insurers in one place. Our experienced experts would help you customise the coverage to cater to the needs of your contract, unorganised, and seasonal workforces.

**Talk to our experts to get a free WC insurance quote today.**

## What e-Shram Covers, and What Employers Still Need to Insure

Let’s complete the picture now. e-Shram offers a verified identity for the unorganised worker, portability between states, and limited insurance cover for accidents. Of course, this is a useful foundation to have, but it does not provide complete protection. It doesn’t remove an employer’s separate statutory liability for workplace injuries, death, or occupational disease. Combining e-Shram registration with a Workmen’s Compensation Policy bridges this gap. This protects the worker and, at the same time, safeguards the business from unplanned financial setbacks.

## FAQs

**Is the e-Shram card free to register?**

Yes, there are no charges for registration on the e-Shram portal. Workers can self-register online or visit a nearby Common Service Centre (CSC) for free assistance.

**Can a worker already covered under EPFO or ESIC also get an e-Shram card?**

Usually, no. The e-Shram scheme is designed for unorganised sector workers only. Hence, those already covered under EPFO or ESIC are not eligible to get an e-Shram card.

**What insurance does the e-Shram card provide?**

PMSBY offers free accidental insurance for workers. They are given ₹2 lakh for accidental death/ complete disability, and ₹1 lakh for partial disability.

**Does the e-Shram card expire or need renewal?**

The e-Shram card never expires, but workers are recommended to keep their profile updated. In particular, they should periodically check and update their contact and bank information (if required) to receive uninterrupted benefits.

**Can an employer help workers register for e-Shram?**

Yes. Employers engaging unorganised/contract workers can encourage workers and help them with e-Shram registration. This way, the employers can help their workforce get access to identity and welfare benefits.

**Does the e-Shram card replace the need for Workmen’s Compensation Insurance?**

No. e-Shram only offers worker identity and limited accidental insurance coverage. However, it doesn’t cover the employer’s legal liability for injuries at the workplace. This gap can be filled by a separate Workmen’s Compensation Insurance only.

[Home](https://eshram.gov.in/) FAQs

#### Frequently Asked Questions

#### [Question 1. What is e-Shram and its purpose?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapseOne1)

e-Shram is a comprehensive National Database of Unorganised Workers (NDUW) launched by the Government of India under the Ministry of Labour & Employment. Its primary purpose is to facilitate delivery of welfare benefits and social security measures to unorganised sector workers across the country. The platform aims to register and provide identity cards to unorganised workers, enabling them to access various government schemes, benefits, and services more efficiently.

#### [Question 2. Where can I access e-Shram services?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapseTwo)

e-Shram services can be accessed through e-Shram portal. You may visit e-Shram portal online at  [http://www.eshram.gov.in.](http://www.eshram.gov.in/) From there, you can register for an account, apply for benefits, update your information, and avail various services offered under the e-Shram initiative.

#### [Question 3. Who are unorganised workers?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapseThree)

Any worker who is a home-based worker, self-employed worker or a wage worker working in the unorganised sector and not a member of ESIC or EPFO, is called an unorganised worker.

#### [Question 4. What is unorganised sector?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapseFour)

Unorganised sector comprises of establishment/ units which are engaged in the production/ sale of goods/ services and employs less than 10 workers. These units are not covered under ESIC & EPFO

#### [Question 5. What is UAN?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapseFive)

UAN or Universal Account Number is a 12 digit number uniquely assigned to each unorganised worker after registration on e-Shram portal. UAN is a permanent number i.e., once assigned, it will remain unchanged for any worker.

#### [Question 6. What should I do if I encounter technical issues with the e-Shram portal?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapseSix)

If you encounter technical issues while using the e-Shram portal, here are steps you can take to resolve them:

- **Check Internet Connection:** Ensure that your internet connection is stable and working properly.

- **Refresh the Page:** Sometimes, simply refreshing the page can resolve minor display or loading issues.

- **Clear Browser Cache:** Clearing your browser's cache and cookies can help resolve issues related to stored data.

- **Try Another Browser:** If the issue persists, try accessing the portal using a different web browser or device.

- **Contact Support:** If none of the above steps resolves the problem, contact the e-Shram portal helpdesk at 14434 for assistance. They can provide further troubleshooting steps or escalate the issue to the technical team, if necessary.

- **Provide Details:** When contacting support, provide details about the issue you are experiencing, including any error messages or specific actions that led to the problem. This information will help them diagnose and resolve the issue more effectively.

- **Keep Updated:** Check for any announcements or updates on the e-Shram portal or official communication channels regarding known technical issues or maintenance periods.


#### [Question 7. How can I stay informed about updates and changes to e-Shram services?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapseSeven)

To stay informed about updates and changes to e-Shram services, you can follow these steps:

- **Official Website:** Visit the official e-Shram website regularly www.eshram.gov.in. Important announcements and updates are posted on the Portal.
- **Social Media:** Follow e-Shram on social media platforms such as Twitter, Facebook, LinkedIn, etc. Updates and announcements are shared on these channels to keep stakeholders informed.

#### [Question 8. Is there any helpdesk I can contact to address my queries?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapseEight)

A dedicated National Help desk has been setup for any queries related to e-Shram registration and grievances. Helpdesk Number is 14434/18008896811 (9.00 AM to 6.00 PM - Daily including Sundays).

#### [Question 9. I am unable to connect to the helpdesk number – 14434/18008896811. What should I do?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapseNine)

Due to high call volume, there may be a scenario where a call could not be connected to helpdesk number 14434/18008896811 (9.00 AM to 6.00 PM - Daily including Sundays). In such case, you are requested to try again after some time or you may raise your grievance through online portal [https://gms.eshram.gov.in.](https://gms.eshram.gov.in/)

#### [Question 10. Are there any income criteria?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapseTen)

There are no income criteria for registering on e-Shram as unorganised worker. However, the worker should not be an income tax payee.

#### [Question 11. Are there any age eligibility criteria to register on e-Shram?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapseTwelve)

A person aged 16 years or above who is engaged in unorganised work may register on eShram, subject to the applicable eligibility conditions.

#### [Question 12. What essential documents are required by the worker to register on e-Shram?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapseThirteen)

Following is required by the worker to register on the e-Shram portal–

- Aadhaar Number
- Aadhaar linked Mobile number.

**Note:** If a worker does not have Aadhaar linked mobile number, he/ she may visit nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) or State Seva Kendra (SSK) and register through biometric authentication.

#### [Question 13. What is the benefit an unorganised worker will get when he/she registers on e-Shram portal?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapseFourteen)

Central Government has developed e-Shram portal which is a centralised database of unorganised workers seeded with Aadhaar. It is envisaged that this portal will be used to facilitate delivery of various social security benefits to unorganised workers. In emergency and national pandemic like situations, this database may be utilised to provide necessary assistance to the eligible unorganised workers.

#### [Question 14. How unorganised workers can register on e-Shram portal?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapseFifteen)

An unorganised worker may register himself/ herself by visiting e-Shram portal or through assisted approach by visiting nearest CSC.

#### [Question 15. Is there any charge the worker must pay for registration on the e-Shram portal?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapseSeventeen)

Registration on e-Shram portal is free. Workers are not required to pay any charges to any registering entity.

#### [Question 16. Does the e-Shram card have validity period?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapseEighteen)

The e-Shram card never expires.

#### [Question 17. Does the worker have to renew the UAN card?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapseNineteen)

No, there is no need to renew the e-Shram card. However, it is recommended to keep the details on the card updated.

#### [Question 18. Who can update workers details on e-Shram?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapseTwenty)

Workers can self-update their details by visiting e-Shram portal or through CSC’s.

#### [Question 19. How can a worker update his/ her personal information on e-Shram?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapseTwenty3)

Updating your personal information on e-Shram can typically be done through the following steps:

- **Login:** Log in to your e-Shram account using your credentials (UAN and OTP).

- **Edit Information:** Look for options to edit or update your personal details such as address, contact information, Banking details etc.

- **Save Changes:** After making the necessary updates, be sure to save the changes by clicking on the "Save" or "Update" button.

- **Verification (if required):** Depending on the information being updated, you may need to verify your changes through a confirmation email or OTP (One-Time Password) sent to your registered mobile number or email address.

#### [Question 20. What is NCO?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapseTwenty4)

NCO stands for “National Classification of Occupation”. It is prepared on the basis of work and skill levels required to execute the work. It is an international practice and uniform across the country. It helps in comparing, classifying, sorting occupations and skill levels.

#### [Question 21. How to select the matching occupation which worker is currently doing?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapseTwenty6)

At the time of registration on eShram Portal, a worker is required to select his activity in the form of occupation which he/ she is currently doing.

#### [Question 22. How occupation is different from skill?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapseTwenty7)

A skill is a learned or natural ability to accomplish a particular task whereas an occupation is a person's usual or principal work or business, especially as a means of earning a living.

#### [Question 23. How my details will be used by the Labour ministry?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapseTwenty8)

e-Shram is a centralised database seeded with Aadhaar. It will be used for facilitating delivery of social security benefits as implemented by Central & State Governments. It will also ensure portability of the social security and welfare benefits to the migrant and construction workers at their working places. It may also be used for providing assistance to the eligible workers during any National crisis like COVID-19 in future.

#### [Question 24. What if after registration on e-Shram the unorganised worker moves to organised sector?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapseTwenty9)

In case if a worker moves to unorganised sector, he/ she will only be entitled for benefits defined for organised sector workers.

#### [Question 25. Whether I must give proof of my date of birth and income?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapse1)

At present there is no need to provide any proof of date of birth and income.

#### [Question 26. Where do I go to solve my grievance?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapse2)

You may call on national helpdesk to register your grievance or register your grievance on e-Shram Grievance portal (gms.eshram.gov.in).

#### [Question 27. Are there any educational qualifications prescribed for registering as an unorganised worker?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapse3)

No, the worker is required to be employed in the gainful employment in the unorganised sector.

#### [Question 28. What are the documents that are to be submitted at the enrolment Centre?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapse4)

Worker is not required to submit any document at the CSC’s. They are required to carry their Aadhaar number & Mobile number for registration.

#### [Question 29. What action is required to be taken by the worker, after attaining the age of 60 years?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapse5)

No action is required merely because the worker turns 60. The UAN remains valid, although eligibility under individual schemes is governed by their own rules.

#### [Question 30. Who will operate the helpdesk/ grievance redressal mechanism?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapse6)

Ministry of Labour & Employment is managing national helpdesk/ grievance redressal mechanism.

#### [Question 31. Is there any interactive map for finding the nearest location of the registration Centre?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapse7)

Yes, please click on the link below to find your nearest CSC Centre for assisted registration - [https://findmycsc.nic.in/csc.](https://findmycsc.nic.in/csc)

#### [Question 32. Can the worker update his/ her photo on e-Shram portal?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapse8)

During the registration, photo is retrieved from Aadhaar services. Therefore provision to update photo on eShram is not available. However, if worker’s photo is updated in Aadhaar, same will be reflected on e-Shram portal as well after completing Aadhaar re-eKYC on eShram.

#### [Question 33. What is occupation?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapse9)

A person's usual or principal work or business, especially as a means of earning a living is called occupation.

#### [Question 34. What is primary occupation?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapse41)

The activity which is major source of income for a worker is called his/ her primary activity/ occupation.

#### [Question 35. What is secondary occupation?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapse42)

Any other activity which is a minor but significant source of income is called secondary activity/ occupation.

#### [Question 36. I have changed my registered mobile number. How can I update my mobile number? or register other mobile number on e-Shram portal?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapse44)

You can login on e-Shram through “Update profile using Aadhaar” under “Already registered” menu and update the new mobile number as your registered number. If you do not have Aadhaar registered mobile number, you may also visit nearest CSC/ SSK’s to update mobile number.

#### [Question 37. Are farmers eligible to register on e-Shram portal?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapse45)

Agriculture labours and landless farmers are eligible for registration in the e-Shram portal.

#### [Question 38. I am 16 years old. Can I register on e-Shram portal?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapse46)

Yes, you are eligible provided you satisfy other registration criteria.

#### [Question 39. Whether my data will get verified from EPFO, ESIC or tax department?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapse47)

Yes, the data will be validated periodically by ESIC, EPFO and income tax departments.

#### [Question 40. What are the details workers can update in e-Shram?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapse48)

Once registered, a worker may update his particulars such as mobile number, current address, occupation, educational qualification, skill types etc. through e-Shram portal or by visiting nearest CSC Centres.

#### [Question 41. What is last date of e-Shram Registration?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapse49)

There is no last date for registration. For the convenience, registration on e-Shram portal is allowed 24 x 7.

#### [Question 42. Are there any financial/ monetary/ cash benefits after registration on e-Shram portal?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapse50)

Right now, only registration is being done through e-Shram.

#### [Question 43. Is e-Shram accessible for individuals with disabilities?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapse51)

Yes, e-Shram aims to be accessible for individuals with disabilities. The platform strives to adhere to accessibility standards to ensure inclusivity for all users.

#### [Question 44. Where can I find announcements or news related to e-Shram?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapse52)

Visit the official e-Shram website regularly [www.eshram.gov.in.](https://www.eshram.gov.in/) Important announcements and updates are often posted on the homepage.

#### [Question 45. How can I provide feedback or suggestions for improving e-Shram services?](https://eshram.gov.in/faqs\#collapse53)

Go to the official e-Shram website. Look for a section or link related to feedback, contact information, or customer helpdesk on 14434. On Mobile app look for Grievance section in Menu tab. Submit your grievance on the link provided.

Ministry of Labour & Employment ![azadi ka amrit mahotsav](https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/photo/2026/sep/ph_9768_20260902_10000501.png) ## Benefits under E-Shram Card Posted On: 02 DEC 2024 7:00PM by PIB Delhi As on 26th November 2024, over 30.42 crore unorganised workers have registered on eShram portal. For providing benefits, eShram portal is integrated / mapped with following portal/schemes: 1. eShram has been integrated with National Career Service (NCS) Portal. An unorganised worker can register on NCS using his/ her Universal Account Number (UAN) and search for suitable job opportunities. An option/ link has also been provided to registrants’ on eShram portal to seamlessly register on NCS. 2. eShram is integrated with Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM). PM-SYM is a pension scheme for unorganised workers who are aged between 18-40 years. It provides a monthly pension of Rs. 3000/- after attaining the age of 60 years. Using UAN any unorganised worker can easily enrol under PMSYM. In the scheme 50 percent of the contribution is borne by the Government of India and the rest is being contributed by the worker. 3. Provision has been added in eShram to capture family details of migrant workers. 4. Provision has been added in eShram to share construction workers’ data with States/ Union Territories to facilitate their registration in respective Building and other Construction Workers (BoCW) boards. 5. To provide skill enhancement and apprenticeship opportunities to unorganised worker, eShram has been integrated with Skill India Digital portal of Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship. 6. eShram is also integrated with myScheme portal. myScheme is a National Platform that aims to offer one-stop search and discovery of the Government schemes. It provides an innovative, technology-based solution to discover scheme information based upon the eligibility of the citizen. In keeping with the vision of the Budget Announcement recently on developing eShram as a One-Stop-Solution for unorganised labour to have access to various social sector schemes, Ministry of Labour and Employment launched the eShram– “One- Stop-Solution” on 21st October 2024. eShram– “One-Stop-Solution” entails integration of different Social Security/ Welfare schemes at single portal i.e., eShram. This enables unorganised workers registered on eShram to access social security schemes and see benefits availed by them so far, through eShram. So far, 12 schemes of different Central Ministries / Departments have already been integrated/ mapped with the eShram including Pradhan Mantri Surakhsa Bima Yojana (PMSBY), Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY), Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana, Prime Minister Street Vendors AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM-SVANidhi), PM Awas Yojana- Urban (PMAY-U), PM Awas Yojana- Gramin (PMAY-G), Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA). This information was given by Union Minister of State for Labour and Employment, Sushri Shobha Karandlaje in a written reply in Lok Sabha today. \\*\\*\\*\*\*\* **Himanshu Pathak** (Release ID: 2079858)Visitor Counter : 20393 Read this release in: [Urdu](https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2079942) , [हिन्दी](https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2079936) | | | --- | | Ministry of Labour & Employment

Benefits under E-Shram Card

Posted On:
02 DEC 2024 7:00PM by PIB Delhi

As on 26th November 2024, over 30.42 crore unorganised workers have registered on eShram portal.
For providing benefits, eShram portal is integrated / mapped with following portal/schemes: 
1. eShram has been integrated with National Career Service (NCS) Portal. An unorganised worker can register on NCS using his/ her Universal Account Number (UAN) and search for suitable job opportunities. An option/ link has also been provided to registrants’ on eShram portal to seamlessly register on NCS.
2. eShram is integrated with Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM). PM-SYM is a pension scheme for unorganised workers who are aged between 18-40 years. It provides a monthly pension of Rs. 3000/- after attaining the age of 60 years. Using UAN any unorganised worker can easily enrol under PMSYM. In the scheme 50 percent of the contribution is borne by the Government of India and the rest is being contributed by the worker. 
3. Provision has been added in eShram to capture family details of migrant workers.
4. Provision has been added in eShram to share construction workers’ data with States/ Union Territories to facilitate their registration in respective Building and other Construction Workers (BoCW) boards.
5. To provide skill enhancement and apprenticeship opportunities to unorganised worker, eShram has been integrated with Skill India Digital portal of Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship.
6. eShram is also integrated with myScheme portal. myScheme is a National Platform that aims to offer one-stop search and discovery of the Government schemes. It provides an innovative, technology-based solution to discover scheme information based upon the eligibility of the citizen.
In keeping with the vision of the Budget Announcement recently on developing eShram as a One-Stop-Solution for unorganised labour to have access to various social sector schemes, Ministry of Labour and Employment launched the eShram– “One- Stop-Solution” on 21st October 2024. eShram– “One-Stop-Solution” entails integration of different Social Security/ Welfare schemes at single portal i.e., eShram. This enables unorganised workers registered on eShram to access social security schemes and see benefits availed by them so far, through eShram.
So far, 12 schemes of different Central Ministries / Departments have already been integrated/ mapped with the eShram including Pradhan Mantri Surakhsa Bima Yojana (PMSBY), Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY), Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana, Prime Minister Street Vendors AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM-SVANidhi), PM Awas Yojana- Urban (PMAY-U), PM Awas Yojana- Gramin (PMAY-G), Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA).
This information was given by Union Minister of State for Labour and Employment, Sushri Shobha Karandlaje in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.
\\*\\*\\*\*\*\*
**Himanshu Pathak**

# E-Shram card apply online 2024: How to check eligibility for pension of Rs 3000 a month, how to apply for E-Shram card

Compiled by

[Tania Jaleel](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/etreporter/author-tania-jaleel-479250007.cms)

, ET Online\|

Oct 19, 2024, 01:30:02 PM IST

![E-Shram card](https://img.etimg.com/thumb/msid-114370622,width-640,resizemode-4,imgsize-1998005/e-shram-card.jpg)

1/6

## E-Shram card

The E-Shram yojana was launched by the Government of India to provide social security for individuals working in unorganized sectors. Moreover, a dedicated E-Shram portal was set up by the government for these workers. The primary objective of the E-Shram portal is to build a comprehensive database of unorganized workers to help them access various government benefits. Those who meet the eligibility criteria for the E-Shram Card 2024 can request an E-Shram card.

This card enables unorganized sector laborers and workers to access numerous benefits, including a pension when they turn 60, life insurance, and financial aid in case of disability. The E-Shram Card 2024 is created to make it easier for unorganized workers to access various new government programs and services through the E-Shram portal. Once your application is approved, you can obtain the E-Shram Card Online 2024 at the eshram.gov.in. This card provides laborers and workers with access to a range of benefits, such as a pension at the age of 60, life insurance, and financial assistance in cases of disability. The E-Shram Card 2024 aims to improve the accessibility of new government programs and services for unorganized workers through the E-Shram portal.

2/6

## E-Shram Card Eligibility

An individual working in the informal sector or any unorganized laborer.

Employees must be between 16 and 59 years old.

Employees need to have a functional mobile number linked to Aadhaar.

Employees should not be subjected to income tax.

ET Online

![How to apply online E-Shram Card](https://img.etimg.com/thumb/msid-114370626,width-640,height-480,resizemode-75,imgsize-2172588/how-to-apply-online-e-shram-card.jpg)

3/6

## How to apply online E-Shram Card

Here are the steps for applying for an EShram Card online at eshram.gov.in:

To get started, visit the self-registration page on the e-Shram portal.

Once there, simply enter your Aadhaar-linked cell phone number and click the “Send OTP” option.

Next, you'll need to agree to the terms and conditions, enter the OTP sent to your mobile device, and provide your Aadhaar number.

Take a moment to review the personal data displayed on the screen and add your address and educational background in the specified fields.

Don't forget to select the relevant skill name, type of business, and nature of work.

After that, another OTP will be sent to your mobile. Once received, click “Verify” to proceed.

Upon completion, you will receive your E-Shram card.

## Benefits Of E-Shram Card

\- Upon reaching the age of 60, a monthly pension of Rs. 3,000 will be provided.

\- In case of a worker sustaining a partial disability due to an accident, they will receive death insurance coverage of Rs. 2,00,000 and financial assistance of Rs. 1,00,000.

\- If the beneficiary passes away due to an accident, the spouse will be eligible to receive all associated benefits.

\- Recipients will be issued a 12-digit UAN which is valid throughout India.

### Public Distribution System

# **Public Distribution System (PDS)**

The Public Distribution System (PDS) evolved as a system of management of scarcity through distribution of foodgrains at affordable prices. Over the years, PDS has become an important part of Government’s policy for management of food economy in the country. PDS is supplemental in nature and is not intended to make available the entire requirement of any of the commodities distributed under it to a household or a section of the society.

PDS is operated under the joint responsibility of the Central and the State/UT Governments. The Central Government, through Food Corporation of India (FCI), has assumed the responsibility for procurement, storage, transportation and bulk allocation of food grains to the State Governments. The operational responsibility including allocation within State, identification of eligible families, issue of Ration Cards and supervision of the functioning of Fair Price Shops (FPSs) etc., rest with the State Governments. Under the PDS, presently the commodities namely wheat, rice, sugar and kerosene are being allocated to the States/UTs for distribution. Some States/UTs also distribute additional items of mass consumption through the PDS outlets such as pulses, edible oils, iodized salt, spices, etc.

## **History of Public Distribution**

### **Public Distribution System in 1960s:**

The public distribution of essential commodities was in existence in the country during the inter-war period. However, PDS, with its focus on distribution of foodgrains in urban scarcity areas, had emanated from the critical food shortages of 1960s. PDS had substantially contributed to the containment of rise in food grains prices and ensured access of food to urban consumers. As the national agricultural production had grown in the aftermath of Green Revolution, the outreach of PDS was extended to tribal blocks and areas of high incidence of poverty in the 1970s and 1980s.

### **Revamped Public Distribution System (RPDS):**

The Revamped Public Distribution System (RPDS) was launched in June, 1992 with a view to strengthen and streamline the PDS as well as to improve its reach in the far-flung, hilly, remote and inaccessible areas where a substantial section of the poor live. It covered 1775 blocks wherein area specific programmes such as the Drought Prone Area Programme(DPAP), Integrated Tribal Development Projects (ITDP), Desert Development Programme (DDP) were being implemented and in certain Designated Hill Areas (DHA) which were identified in consultation with State Governments for special focus. Food grains for distribution in RPDS areas were issued to the States at 50 paise below the Central Issue Price. The scale of issue was up to 20 kg per card.

The RPDS included area approach for ensuring effective reach of the PDS commodities, their delivery by State Governments at the doorstep of FPSs in the identified areas, additional ration cards to the left out families, infrastructure requirements like additional Fair Price Shops, storage capacity etc. and additional commodities such as tea, salt, pulses, soap, etc. for distribution through PDS outlets.

### **Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS):**

In June, 1997, the Government of India launched the Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS) with focus on the poor. Under the PDS, States were required to formulate and implement foolproof arrangements for identification of the poor for delivery of foodgrains and for its distribution in a transparent and accountable manner at the FPS level.

The scheme, when introduced, was intended to benefit about 6 crore poor families for whom a quantity of about 72 lakh tonnes of food grains was earmarked annually. The identification of the poor under the scheme was done by the States as per State-wise poverty estimates of the Planning Commission for 1993-94 based on the methodology of the "Expert Group on estimation of proportion and number of poor” chaired by Late Prof Lakdawala. The allocation of food grains to the States/UTs was made on the basis of average consumption in the past i.e. average annual off-take of food grains under the PDS during the past ten years at the time of introduction of TPDS.

The quantum of food grains in excess of the requirement of Below Poverty Line (BPL) families was provided to the State as ‘transitory allocation’ for which a quantum of 103 lakh tonnes of food grains was earmarked annually. Over and above the TPDS allocation, additional allocation to States was also given. The transitory allocation was intended for continuation of benefit of subsidized food grains to the population Above the Poverty Line (APL) as any sudden withdrawal of benefits existing under PDS from them was not considered desirable. The transitory allocation was issued at prices, which were subsidized but were higher than the prices for the BPL quota of food grains.

Keeping in view the consensus on increasing the allocation of food grains to BPL families, and to better target the food subsidy, Government of India increased the allocation to BPL families from 10 kg to 20 kg of food grains per family per month at 50% of the economic cost and allocation to APL families at economic cost w.e.f. 1.4.2000. The allocation of APL families was retained at the same level as at the time of introduction of TPDS but the Central Issue Prices (CIPs) for APL were fixed at 100% of economic cost from that date so that the entire consumer subsidy could be directed to the benefit of the BPL population. However, the CIPs fixed in July and December, 2000 for BPL & AAY respectively and in July, 2002 for APL were not revised upwards since then even though procurement cost have gone up considerably.

The number of BPL families was increased w.e.f. 1.12.2000 by shifting the base to the population projections of the Registrar General as on 1.3.2000 instead of the earlier population projection of 1995. With this increase, the total number of BPL families came to 652.03 lakh as against 596.23 lakh families originally estimated when TPDS was introduced in June 1997.

Under the TPDS, the end retail price was fixed by the States/UTs after taking into account margin for wholesalers/ retailers, transportation charges, levies local taxes etc. The States were earlier requested to issue food-grains at a difference of not more than 50 paise per kg over and above the CIP for BPL families. However, since 2001, flexibility was given to States/UTs in the matter of fixing the retail issue prices by removing the restriction of 50 paise per kg over and above the CIP for distribution of food grains under TPDS.

### **Antodaya Anna Yojana (AAY)**

AAY was a step in the direction of making TPDS aim at reducing hunger among the poorest segments of the BPL population. A National Sample Survey Exercise pointed towards the fact that about 5% of the total population in the country sleeps without two square meals a day. This section of the population could be called as "hungry”. In order to make TPDS more focused and targeted towards this category of population, the "Antyodaya Anna Yojana” (AAY) was launched in December, 2000 for one crore poorest of the poor families.

AAY involved identification of one crore poorest of the poor families from amongst the number of BPL families covered under TPDS within the States and providing them food grains at a highly subsidized rate of Rs.2/- per kg. for wheat and Rs.3/- per kg for rice. The States/UTs were required to bear the distribution cost, including margin to dealers and retailers as well as the transportation cost. Thus the entire food subsidy was passed on to the consumers under the scheme.

The scale of issue that was initially 25 kg per family per month was increased to 35 kg per family per month with effect from 1st April 2002.

**The AAY Scheme has since expanded to cover 2.50 crore poorest of the poor households as follows:**

### **1\. First Expansion**

The AAY Scheme was expanded in 2003-04 by adding another 50 lakh BPL households headed by widows or terminally ill persons or disabled persons or persons aged 60 years or more with no assured means of subsistence or societal support. Order to this effect was issued on 3rd June, 2003. With this increase, 1.5 crore (i.e. 23% of BPL) families were covered under the AAY.

### **2\. Second Expansion**

As announced in the Union Budget 2004-05, the AAY was further expanded by another 50 lakh BPL families by including, inter alia, all households at the risk of hunger. Order to this effect was issued on 3rd August 2004. In order to identify these households, the guidelines stipulated the following criteria:-

a) Landless agriculture labourers, marginal farmers, rural artisans /craftsmen, such as potters, tanners, weavers, blacksmiths, carpenters, slum dwellers and persons earning their livelihood on daily basis in the informal sector like porters, coolies, rickshaw pullers, hand cart pullers, fruit and flower sellers, snake charmers, rag pickers, cobblers, destitute and other similar categories in both rural and urban areas.

b) Households headed by widows or terminally ill persons/disabled persons/ persons aged 60 years or more with no assured means of subsistence or societal support.

c) Widows or terminally ill persons or disabled persons or persons aged 60 years or more or single women or single men with no family or societal support or assured means of subsistence.

d) All primitive tribal households.

### **3\. Third Expansion**

As announced in the Union Budget 2005-06, the AAY was expanded to cover another 50 lakh BPL households thus increasing its coverage to 2.5 crore households (i.e. 38% of BPL). Order to this effect was issued on 12th May, 2005.
